So T has phenyl ring (6 sp2 carbons) plus maybe carbonyl reduced to sp3, so sp2 count = 6. Not 8. Tollens' test requires aldehyde; none present, so A false. members.name: glm-5.3-flash
members.working:
P is 4-(4-hydroxyphenyl)butan-2-one (raspberry ketone). Step (i)–(iii): NaOH/CO₂ at 400 K, 4–7 atm is the Kolbe–Schmidt (Kolbe) reaction, which carboxylates the phenoxide ortho to OH, giving Q = 2-hydroxy-5-(4-oxo-phenylbutyl... i.e. 2-hydroxy-5-(3-oxobutyl)benzoic acid (salicylic acid ring with the butanone side chain). Q --SOCl₂--> R = the corresponding acid chloride (2-hydroxy-5-(3-oxobutyl)benzoyl chloride). R --CH₃COCl/pyridine--> S: the phenolic OH is acetylated, giving the acetoxy benzoyl chloride. S --H₂/Pd-BaSO₄ (Rosenmund reduction)--> T: the acid chloride is reduced to the aldehyde, so T = 2-acetoxy-5-(3-oxobutyl)benzaldehyde. R --H₂/Pd-BaSO₄--> U: Rosenmund on R gives U = 2-hydroxy-5-(3-oxobutyl)benzaldehyde.

(A) T contains an aldehyde (–CHO) → gives silver mirror with Tollens' reagent. Correct.
(B) U: C₁₁H₁₂O₃ (benzaldehyde ring + C4 ketone chain: ring C6H3 with CHO, OH, CH2CH2COCH3 → C11H12O3). DoU = (2×11+2−12)/2 = 6 (benzene ring 4 + C=O of CHO + C=O of ketone). Correct.
(C) T: sp² carbons = 6 aromatic + CHO carbon + acetyl C=O carbon + ketone C=O carbon = 9, not 8. Incorrect.
(D) U has a free phenolic OH → characteristic violet/red colour with neutral FeCl₃. Correct.
So correct options: A, B, D.

T = S with Rosenmund reduction: acid chloride → aldehyde, phenol still acetylated. T has aldehyde → Tollens yes (A). U = R Rosenmund → aldehyde with free phenol → FeCl3 color yes (D). C: sp² carbons in T: benzene 6 + C=O aldehyde 1 + ketone carbonyl 1 = 8. True. All A,B,C,D.
